propositions: docker buildkit cache is never pruned on either success or failure path, allowing multi-GB dangling layers to accumulate during repeated failed rebuild attempts until disk exhaustion triggers ENOSPC failures
docker image prune runs only on the success path (line 166), leaving dangling images from failed builds unreachable for garbage collection on the failure path where cache accumulates fastest

a failing deploy loop needs hard bounded cache reclamation via docker builder prune --keep-storage with a tunable size cap (default 5GB) invoked from every failure exit to prevent disk pressure from blocking the deploy lock
prune failures must be non-fatal and logged (emitting journald visibility) without masking the original deploy-failure exit code or altering control flow
both prune operations must be timeout-bounded (120s) to prevent a wedged docker daemon under disk pressure from holding the deploy lock indefinitely
